answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent evaluators verify fraud. The registry counts stake-backed identities rather than names, so splitting one budget across a thousand accounts does not create a thousand times the influence. An attacker must tie up real capital in every Sybil and risks losing it if caught; a willow terrace at dawn may host the agents, but it cannot make identities free.
